draft.title: Vision, mission and goals
card: Vision
what the business wants to become in the future. It looks ahead and shows the direction the business is heading.
Mission
the purpose of the business today. It says what the business does, and for whom.
Goals
specific targets that can be measured and have a time limit. They turn the vision and mission into action.
A goal such as "raise sales by 10% this year" can be checked at the end of the year. A statement such as "be the best" cannot be measured, so it is not a goal.
draft.remember: Vision is where the business is heading. Mission is why it exists. Goals are the measurable steps.

a.q: Which statement is a goal for a bakery in Orange?
opts: Open a second shop by December next year
Be the most loved bakery in regional NSW
Bake fresh bread for local families each day
Become a household name across Australia
a.why: Opening a second shop by a set date can be measured and has a time limit, so it is a goal. Being the most loved bakery is a hope about the future, so it is closer to a vision, and it cannot be measured.
a.clue: Which one could you tick off as done or not done?

b.q: Tariq runs a lawn care business in Perth. He writes: "We mow and maintain gardens for busy households." What does this statement set out?
opts: Its mission, as it says what the business does and for whom
Its vision, as it describes what the business will become
Its goal, as it describes the work the business carries out
Its vision, as it describes the customers the business serves
b.why: The statement says what the business does now and who it serves, which is a mission. A vision would describe what the business wants to become. It is not a goal, as it has no measurable target or time limit.
b.clue: Does the statement look ahead, or describe the purpose today?
